description: A Bot's routines, a page of the right-hand side panel: work the Bot is given on a schedule. They are kept with the Bot on its host, which gives the Bot a turn with the routine's task as each comes due (as if you had said it), whether or not Baude is open; each run shows in the Bot's chat as a turn of its own. A routine missed while the host was off runs once when it is back. Only exists while the open chat is a Bot; otherwise the tab is hidden, and if it was shown the panel falls back to Meta.
opens: the 'Routines' tab (alarm-clock icon) in the side panel's switcher, visible only while the open chat is a Bot

parts.name: tab
parts.shows: Switcher tab with an alarm-clock icon and the label 'Routines'; present only for a Bot chat.

parts.name: header row
parts.shows: A row at the top with empty space at the left (the page's name is the tab's) and a flat plus button at the right, tooltip 'New routine'.

actions.does: opens the New Routine dialog (see 'routine dialog')

parts.name: list
parts.shows: A boxed list of the Bot's routines in the order its host keeps them, scrolling, no selection. Empty: the centred dim text 'No routines yet'. The list is read when the chat is opened, when a turn of the Bot ends, every 30 seconds while the page is shown, and after each change here.

parts.name: routine row
parts.shows: Title: the routine's name ('Routine' if it has none). Subtitle on one line, parts joined with ' · ': the schedule, then either 'paused' or 'next <time>', then 'last <time>' if it has run, then the error text if its last run could not be made. Schedule wording: 'every hour', 'every 2 hours' (whole hours from 2 up), 'every <n> minutes' (otherwise, including 90), or '<days> at <HH:MM>' where days is 'weekdays', 'weekends', 'every day' or the day names joined with ', ' (Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat, Sun). A time is HH:MM on the host's clock if it is today, else 'Mon 03 Nov 14:00'; a time that is not known is 'never'. At the end of the row, in order: a switch, a Run now button (play icon), a Change button (pencil icon), a Delete button (trash icon). Row text is escaped, never markup.

actions.does: on = running, off = paused (tooltip 'Turn off to pause'); saved to the host at once; turning it back on works out the next run afresh
the host gives the Bot a turn with the routine's task now
opens the Change Routine dialog filled with it
deletes the routine on the host at once (no confirmation)

parts.name: message line
parts.shows: A dim wrapping line under the list (10 px margins), hidden unless something failed: "Couldn't load the routines.", "Couldn't run the routine.", "Couldn't save the routine.", "Couldn't delete the routine."; the host's reason is in its tooltip. It goes away after the next successful answer.

parts.name: routine dialog
parts.shows: An Adw alert dialog headed 'New Routine' (or 'Change Routine'), default response Save, with Cancel and Save (suggested) buttons. Content (scrolls if the window is short, 440 px at most): a text field with the placeholder 'Name'; the label 'Task' over a card-style multi-line text box (at least 110 px tall, wrapping) for what the Bot is to do; a drop-down with 'Every' or 'At a time of day' (a new routine starts on 'Every'; one that has a time starts on 'At a time of day'). With 'Every': a number box and a unit drop-down 'minutes' / 'hours'; minutes 5 to 999, hours 1 to 744 (a month); a routine runs no more often than every 5 minutes and no less often than monthly; a new routine defaults to 1 hour; an existing one whose period is whole hours shows hours. With 'At a time of day': the label 'Times in <zone>' (the host's time zone, e.g. 'Times in GMT') or 'Times on the host's clock' when the zone is not known, a time field (placeholder 'HH:MM', default 09:00), and a row of seven toggle buttons Mon to Sun (a new routine has Mon to Fri on). The host checks the routine when it is saved: a task is required (the name defaults to the first line of the task, 40 characters), the time must be HH:MM, at least one day must be on.

actions.does: saves the routine on the host (a new one is made; a changed one keeps its id and last-run time, its next run is kept unless its schedule changed); if the host rejects it, the message line says 'Couldn't save the routine.' with the reason as its tooltip

states.name: paused routine
states.shows: Switch off, subtitle '<schedule> · paused' (no next time)

states.name: failed last run
states.shows: The error text is the last part of the subtitle; the next run is still worked out
